name: SendGridEmail
title: Send Email
description: Send an email through SendGrid, as plain text or HTML
whenToUse: Send an email to a recipient inbox: a notification, report, confirmation or outreach message addressed to an email address. Runs as a pipeline step rather than a tool an agent calls, and reaches a mailbox rather than a chat channel or the client UI, so it is the wrong step when the message should appear in a conversation the user is already in.

inputs.name: signal
inputs.description: Trigger signal from the upstream node

outputs.name: sent
outputs.description: True when SendGrid accepted the message for delivery

outputs.name: messageId
outputs.description: SendGrid's message id, for looking the send up in Activity

from.title: From
from.description: Sender address. Must be a verified sender or belong to an authenticated domain in your SendGrid account, or the send is rejected.

to.title: To
to.description: Recipient address. Separate multiple with commas.

body.title: Body
body.description: The message itself, as plain text or HTML depending on Body Type

bodyType.title: Body Type
bodyType.description: Send the body as plain text, or as HTML with links and formatting

autoLinkUrls.title: Auto-link URLs
autoLinkUrls.description: In HTML mode, turn bare URLs in the body into clickable links. A body that is already HTML keeps its own line breaks; a plain one has its newlines converted.

gaMeasurementId.title: GA Measurement ID
gaMeasurementId.description: Google Analytics id (G-XXXXXXXXXX). Adds a 1x1 pixel to the HTML body so opens are counted. Leave blank for no open tracking.

utmSource.title: UTM Source
utmSource.description: Tags every link in the body, e.g. "newsletter". Leave blank and no UTM parameters are added at all; the other three only apply once this is set.

utmCampaign.title: UTM Campaign
utmCampaign.description: e.g. "april-outreach". Also used as the open-tracking label.

utmContent.title: UTM Content
utmContent.description: e.g. "cta-button", to tell links apart in an A/B test

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: email
package.packageFile:
name: email
displayName: Email
version: 2.0.0
description: Send email over HTTP

# THE PROVIDER CHANGED, and that is the whole reason this package could become a manifest.
#
# Until 2026-07-29 this was Microsoft 365 over SMTP, via nodemailer. SMTP is a socket
# protocol with a stateful conversation (EHLO, AUTH, MAIL FROM, RCPT TO, DATA), and no
# amount of manifest will ever speak it: the format describes REQUESTS, and SMTP is not one.
# The node was not "not yet migrated", it was unmigratable as written.
#
# SendGrid sends the same email as ONE POST with a JSON body, so the node becomes a
# description of a request and the capability question disappears. That is a real product
# change (a different vendor, a different account, different deliverability) rather than a
# refactor, so it is recorded here rather than buried in a diff.
#
# The old node is at _legacy/nodes/email. Workflows keep working until they are repointed:
# the type is deliberately NOT reused (SendEmail → SendGridEmail), because a saved workflow
# stores the type string and silently swapping the transport under it would change where
# every existing email came from without anyone choosing that.

category: communication

allowedHosts:
  # api.sendgrid.com is global; api.eu.sendgrid.com is the EU data residency host. Both are
  # listed because the choice is an account property, not a per-workflow one, and a node
  # that could only reach the global host would fail for an EU tenant with a refused-host
  # error that says nothing about data residency.
  - api.sendgrid.com
  - api.eu.sendgrid.com

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.6.0"
  credential: [bearer]
  transport: [json, headers]

credentials.sendgridCredential.yaml:
# SendGrid authenticates with a single API key as a bearer token.
#
# No username/password pair like the retired M365 credential: that one carried a MAILBOX's
# own login, so the node signed in AS a person and the "from" address was forced to be that
# mailbox. A SendGrid key belongs to the account and can send as any VERIFIED sender, which
# is why `from` is a required config field here rather than defaulting to the credential.

name: sendgridCredential
displayName: SendGrid
description: >-
  SendGrid API key with Mail Send permission. Create it under Settings → API Keys; a
  Restricted Access key with only "Mail Send" is enough and is the safer choice.

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your SendGrid API key. Starts with SG.
    placeholder: "SG."

  - name: host
    displayName: API Host
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    # A per-ACCOUNT fact, not a per-workflow one, so it belongs on the credential rather
    # than in every node's config. Blank means the global host.
    description: >-
      Leave blank for the global endpoint. Set to api.eu.sendgrid.com only if your account
      was created under EU data residency, which is chosen at account level and cannot be
      changed later.
    placeholder: api.sendgrid.com

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml's order.

# The request settled, which for this endpoint IS the answer: a 202 means SendGrid has
# queued the message. There is no delivery confirmation to wait for, and a node that tried
# to report one would be inventing it.
- emit: sent
  value: "return true"

# `x-message-id` is the handle SendGrid's Activity feed is searched by. Lower-cased because
# the headers transport normalises key case, so this does not depend on how the vendor
# capitalised it on the day.
#
# Falls back to empty rather than undefined: the output is declared a string, and a
# downstream template rendering the word "undefined" into a log line is worse than a blank.
- emit: messageId
  value: "return response['x-message-id'] || ''"
files.config.yaml:
# Transcribed from the retired node's configSchema, minus `provider`.
#
# `provider` was an enum with exactly ONE value ("microsoft365"), which is a dropdown that
# cannot be changed: it described the package rather than the step. The package now names its
# vendor, so the field has nothing left to say.

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [from, to, subject, body]
  properties:
    from:
      type: string
      title: From
      description: >-
        Sender address. Must be a verified sender or belong to an authenticated domain in
        your SendGrid account, or the send is rejected.
      default: ""
      ui:field: template

    to:
      type: string
      title: To
      description: Recipient address. Separate multiple with commas.
      default: ""
      ui:field: template

    subject:
      type: string
      title: Subject
      description: The subject line
      default: ""
      ui:field: template

    body:
      type: string
      title: Body
      description: The message itself, as plain text or HTML depending on Body Type
      default: ""
      ui:field: template

    bodyType:
      type: string
      title: Body Type
      description: Send the body as plain text, or as HTML with links and formatting
      default: text
      enum: [text, html]
      enumNames: [Plain Text, HTML]

    autoLinkUrls:
      type: boolean
      title: Auto-link URLs
      description: >-
        In HTML mode, turn bare URLs in the body into clickable links. A body that is already
        HTML keeps its own line breaks; a plain one has its newlines converted.
      default: true
      "ui:widget": toggle
      "ui:dependencies": { bodyType: html }

    gaMeasurementId:
      type: string
      title: GA Measurement ID
      description: >-
        Google Analytics id (G-XXXXXXXXXX). Adds a 1x1 pixel to the HTML body so opens are
        counted. Leave blank for no open tracking.
      default: ""
      "ui:dependencies": { bodyType: html }

    utmSource:
      type: string
      title: UTM Source
      description: >-
        Tags every link in the body, e.g. "newsletter". Leave blank and no UTM parameters are
        added at all; the other three only apply once this is set.
      default: ""
      ui:field: template
      "ui:dependencies": { bodyType: html }

    utmMedium:
      type: string
      title: UTM Medium
      description: e.g. "email"
      default: ""
      ui:field: template
      "ui:dependencies": { bodyType: html }

    utmCampaign:
      type: string
      title: UTM Campaign
      description: e.g. "april-outreach". Also used as the open-tracking label.
      default: ""
      ui:field: template
      "ui:dependencies": { bodyType: html }

    utmContent:
      type: string
      title: UTM Content
      description: e.g. "cta-button", to tell links apart in an A/B test
      default: ""
      ui:field: template
      "ui:dependencies": { bodyType: html }

    cc:
      type: string
      title: CC
      description: Copied recipients, comma-separated
      default: ""
      ui:field: template

    bcc:
      type: string
      title: BCC
      description: Blind-copied recipients, comma-separated
      default: ""
      ui:field: template
"ui:order":
  [from, to, cc, bcc, subject, bodyType, body, autoLinkUrls, utmSource, utmMedium, utmCampaign, utmContent, gaMeasurementId]
files.interface.yaml:
inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    required: true
    description: Trigger signal from the upstream node

outputs:
  - name: sent
    type: boolean
    description: True when SendGrid accepted the message for delivery

  # SendGrid returns the id in a HEADER, not the body, and the body is empty on success.
  # The retired node surfaced nodemailer's SMTP message id here; this is the equivalent
  # handle for tracing a message in SendGrid's Activity feed.
  - name: messageId
    type: string
    description: SendGrid's message id, for looking the send up in Activity

credentials:
  - name: sendgridCredential
    required: true
    displayName: SendGrid
files.node.yaml:
# Transcribed from _legacy/nodes/email/src/SendEmail, with SMTP replaced by SendGrid's REST
# API. Every body transform the old node performed (auto-linking, UTM injection, the open
# pixel) is reproduced as an expression; see api/run.yaml for each one.

type: SendGridEmail

# NOT the old `SendEmail` type. A saved workflow stores the type string, so reusing it would
# silently move every existing email from a Microsoft 365 mailbox to a SendGrid account
# without anyone choosing that, and the first sign would be a deliverability change nobody
# could trace. A new type makes repointing a decision someone makes on the canvas.

kind: PromiseNode

name: Send Email
category: Communication
color: "#1A82E2"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1775377626/gravity/icons/microsoft365.png

description: Send an email through SendGrid, as plain text or HTML

whenToUse: >-
  Send an email to a recipient inbox: a notification, report, confirmation or outreach
  message addressed to an email address. Runs as a pipeline step rather than a tool an agent
  calls, and reaches a mailbox rather than a chat channel or the client UI, so it is the
  wrong step when the message should appear in a conversation the user is already in.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
#
# Deliberately NOT `true`, despite sending mail on the account's behalf. The dangerous
# property of this node is the SENDER, which is fixed by the credential and the verified
# sender list, not by who triggered the run. A workflow that should only mail for signed-in
# people says so with the instance toggle, which is where that decision actually belongs.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # NEVER cacheable: sending is the side effect. A cached answer would report a successful
  # send for a message that was never delivered, which is the worst possible lie for a node
  # whose entire purpose is that something left the building.
  cacheable: false

  # The same fact, stated positively so the ENGINE can act on it: mail that has reached a
  # mailbox has no inverse. Test runs withhold this node and trace what it would have sent,
  # because a build calls runTest after every stage and each one would otherwise put a real
  # message in a real person's inbox.
  emitsExternally: true
files.test.yaml:
# Sends a REAL email. There is no dry-run mode on this endpoint, so `to` should be an inbox
# you own and `from` must be a verified sender on the account the key belongs to.
#
# Asserts the SHAPE, not the words: a message id exists and is SendGrid's, rather than the
# empty string the events row falls back to when the header is missing. That fallback is the
# thing worth testing, because it is what turns "the header moved" into a silent blank.

testData:
  config:
    from: "{{ env.SENDGRID_FROM }}"
    to: "{{ env.SENDGRID_TO }}"
    subject: Unoverse node test
    bodyType: html
    body: |-
      A test from the SendGrid manifest node.

      Bare link, which auto-linking should turn into an anchor: https://unoverse.ai
    autoLinkUrls: true
    utmSource: node-test
    utmMedium: email
  inputs:
    signal: {}
  expect:
    sent: "return output.sent === true"
    messageId: "return typeof output.messageId === 'string' && output.messageId.length > 0"
